questions.q: Why does a wide table (many fields) slow down queries, per this lesson, even when a query only touches a few of those fields?
options: ServiceNow blocks queries on tables with more than 20 fields
Row storage and I/O read the row's data regardless of which columns the query asked for, so width still costs something
Wide tables cannot be indexed at all
Field count has no actual effect on query performance
questions.explain: Width isn't free — more data per row means more to read per row, even for a query that filters on just a few fields.

questions.q: What ongoing cost does every indexed field add, beyond helping queries run faster?
options: No additional cost — indexes are free once created
Maintenance overhead on every insert and update to that table, not just on reads
A one-time cost paid only when the index is first created
Indexes only affect table width, not write performance
questions.explain: Every indexed field has to be maintained on every write to the table — a cost paid on every record, forever, not just once.

questions.q: Per this lesson, when does it make sense to extend an existing base table like task rather than build a new, unrelated table?
options: Always, since extension is mechanically easier
Never, since extension always hurts performance
When the new data genuinely is a kind of the base table's own meaning, and you accept the shared table growing wider
Only when the new table will have fewer than 100 records
questions.explain: Extension is right when the data truly belongs under the base table's meaning — but it does mean the shared table absorbs the new fields' width.

questions.q: What does "designing for ten million records, not a thousand" actually mean in practice?
options: Buying more server hardware before building the table
Asking at design time what the table looks like after years of real production use, not just how it behaves with current test data
Limiting every table to exactly ten million records
Avoiding reference fields in favor of free text
questions.explain: A design that performs fine with a thousand test records can behave very differently at real multi-year production volume — the architect's job is anticipating that.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend reference fields over long free-text fields for categorical data?
options: Free-text fields are always invalid in ServiceNow
Reference fields index and filter far better at volume than string fields
Reference fields never add to table width
There is no real performance difference between the two
questions.explain: For genuinely categorical data, a reference field performs better under filtering and indexing at scale than a long text field.
